\section[o ficheiro]{o ficheiro — the computer file}

\label{lesson:PT-C398-ficheiro}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to uninstall, then the Portuguese for to update.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o ficheiro}
\textbf{o ficheiro} — \textquotedblleft{}the computer file\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Perdi o ficheiro com o trabalho todo.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I lost the file with all the work.}
\end{quote}

European Portuguese; in Brazil \emph{o arquivo}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ficheiro} is built on \emph{ficha} \textquotedblleft{}index card\textquotedblright{}, borrowed from French \emph{fiche} \textquotedblleft{}peg, mark\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), on \emph{ficher} \textquotedblleft{}to fasten\textquotedblright{}, which is usually traced to Latin \emph{fīgere} \textquotedblleft{}to fix\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{o ficheiro}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{o ficheiro}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{o ficheiro}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for to uninstall, then the Portuguese for to update, then say \emph{o ficheiro} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does o ficheiro mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The computer file\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[copiar]{copiar — to copy}

\label{lesson:PT-C398-copiar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to update, then the Portuguese for the computer file.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: copiar}
\textbf{copiar} — \textquotedblleft{}to copy\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Copiei as fotos para o portátil.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I copied the photos to the laptop.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Copiar num exame} — to cheat in an exam.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{copiar} is built on \emph{cópia} \textquotedblleft{}copy\textquotedblright{}, from Medieval Latin \emph{copia} \textquotedblleft{}transcript\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from Latin \emph{cōpia} \textquotedblleft{}plenty, abundance\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short): a copy multiplies a text.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{copiar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{copiar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{copiar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for to update, then the Portuguese for the computer file, then say \emph{copiar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[guardar]{guardar — to save (a file); to keep; to put away}

\label{lesson:PT-C398-guardar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the computer file, then the Portuguese for to copy.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: guardar}
\textbf{guardar} — \textquotedblleft{}to save (a file); to keep; to put away\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Guardei o ficheiro antes de desligar o computador.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I saved the file before switching off the computer.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Guardar um segredo} — to keep a secret.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{guardar} is inherited from Medieval Latin \emph{wardāre}, which took it from Frankish \emph{wardōn} \textquotedblleft{}to keep, to guard, to save\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[o anexo]{o anexo — the attachment; the annex}

\label{lesson:PT-C398-anexo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to copy, then the Portuguese for to save.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o anexo}
\textbf{o anexo} — \textquotedblleft{}the attachment; the annex\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O anexo é muito grande para enviar.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The attachment is too big to send.}
\end{quote}

Also an annex to a building or a document.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{anexo} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{annexus} \textquotedblleft{}a connection\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from \emph{annectere} \textquotedblleft{}to tie on\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{nectere} \textquotedblleft{}to bind\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
